short: A weak, sheltered western emperor whose thirty-year reign presided over the loss of Britain and Rome itself.
full:
Honorius was made co-Augustus by his father Theodosius I on 23 January 393 CE and became sole ruler of the western empire at the age of ten on his father's death in January 395 CE, governed in practice by the general Stilicho until Stilicho's execution in 408 CE on suspicion of treachery. Honorius himself took little active role in government, retreating to the fortified marshes of Ravenna, which he made his capital in 402 CE.

His reign saw Roman authority effectively withdraw from Britain around 410 CE and the western field army fail repeatedly to contain Gothic and other groups now settled inside imperial territory. Honorius died of illness at Ravenna on 15 August 423 CE, leaving no son and a western empire whose military and financial base had been permanently weakened.
